Row.Text: Economics

Borrow from other civilizations or a bond market and pay it back from what the Gold brings in, lend to a neighbour in trouble, pick a tax level as a policy card, and watch an auto-loan guard keep you clear of the game's negative-balance penalties. Missed payments cost you, default costs more, and repudiating a debt keeps the Gold at the price of your name. Single-player.
Loans

Whether civilizations can borrow from each other and, later, from a bond market, within a limit set by income. Off turns the whole loan system off: no Gold moves and the Economics screen shows balances only.
Off
Nobody borrows or lends. The Economics screen shows balances only.
On
Loans between civilizations open with Moneylending, the bond market with Public debt.
Auto-loan guard

When your treasury is about to fall below the line where the game starts taking amenities, the guard takes out an emergency loan for you, up to a cap of ten turns of your income. You can also switch it on the Loans tab.
Off
You borrow only when you ask to. The game's penalties for a negative balance apply as usual.
On
An emergency loan covers a shortfall before the game's penalties start, until the cap is reached. You're told once when it is.
AI borrowing and lending
Whether the computer players take part: borrowing when they run short, lending when they're flush, restructuring an overdue loan, and now and then repudiating a debt to an enemy.
Off
Only you borrow and lend. The computer players keep their treasuries as the base game runs them.
On
Computer players borrow, lend, restructure and repudiate by the same rules you play under.
Rates
Scales every interest rate in the game, the rate cap included. Standard is 3 percent a turn in Antiquity, 2 in Exploration and 1.5 in Modern before standing and relationship adjust it.
Low
Three quarters of the standard rates. Borrowing is cheap and lending pays less.
Standard
The rates the mod is balanced around.
High
A quarter above the standard rates. Debt bites sooner and lending pays more.
Taxes

Adds the tax policy cards: Light Taxation, Heavy Taxation and War Levy. Each trades Gold against happiness in one of your ordinary policy slots, and the computer players choose among them as they do any card.
Off
The tax cards aren't in the game.
On
The three tax cards appear in the policy list as their civics unlock them.
Economic stages
Whether each part opens with the tech or civic that historically brought it in: loans between civilizations with Moneylending, the bond market and longer terms with Public debt.
Off
Every part is open from the start of its age.
On
A part opens for a civilization when it reaches the stage's tech or civic. With the option off everything is open from the start of its age.
